text: The assembly will hear an address by his
excellency
Zadir Sapavov,
president of the Kygis Republic.
I request protocol to escort his
excellency and invite him to address the
assembly.
Mr. President, Mr. Secretary General,
distinguished heads of delegations,
ladies and gentlemen, at the outset of
my speech, I would like to sincerely
congratulate Mr.
Rahman on being elected as the president
of the 81st session of the United
Nations General Assembly and wish him
further success.
As you are all aware, last year the
international community marked the 80th
anniversary of the United Nations.
For 80 years, this unique global
organization has been standing at the
forefront of safeguarding peace,
security, and development. Although our
organization brings together all
countries of the world and serves as the
principal platform for international
cooperation, wars and tensions still
persist in various regions.
Iron conflicts and humanitarian crisis
in different parts of the world
including Ukraine, Iran, Sudan, and
Palestine demonstrate the complexity of
the current international environment
and require all of us to work together
to strengthen peace, security,
and sustainable development.
Kyrgyzstan is a country that believes in
the power of dialogue and the peaceful
settlement of conflicts.
Our country stands ready to serve as a
mediator in addressing complex and
contentious issues. In recent years,
Central Asia has clearly demonstrated to
the world its ability to resolve complex
interstate issues peacefully.
Today, Central Asia is becoming an
example of constructive interstate
cooperation as well as economic,
infrastructural, and technological
development.
In this regard,
we are ready to share the experience we
have accumulated along this path.
Distinguished heads of delegations, for
the first time in its history,
Kyrgyzstan has been elected as a member
of the United Nations Security Council
for the 2027 2028 term. Taking this
opportunity, I would like to express my
profound gratitude to all countries that
supported our candidacy. The support of
142 member states not only confirms
Kungasan's readiness to contribute to
international affairs but also
demonstrates the growing role of the
Central Asian region in international
relations. This achievement is clear
evidence that even small states can make
a meaningful contribution to addressing
global challenges. We fully understand
that membership in the security council
is not a privilege or award. It is a
great responsibility.
One year ago, standing at this stage, I
started with confident that Kyrgyzstan
is among those states whose experience
enables them to put forward substantive
issues for consideration by the Security
Council. We do not forget the promises
we have made and will make every effort
to implement them fully.
Therefore, I would like to reiterate
Kyrgystan firmly adheres to
international law, justice, and the
protection of human rights and supports
the multilateral system based on mutual
respect, balance of interest, and
responsibility toward future
generations.
We intend to work closely with every
country and remain committed to
productive cooperation.
Distinguished colleagues,
as you all may know, since the
establishment of the United Nations in
1945, its member states and leaders have
attempted to undertake systematic
reforms.
Reforms have ranged from expanding the
membership of the security council to
modernizing mechanisms of governance,
peacekeeping, and the protection of
human rights.
These initiatives continue to be
actively discussed at the international
level.
However, despite numerous efforts and
years of discussion, the institutional
structure of our organization continues
to face various challenges. Therefore, I
believe that expanding the membership of
the security council is one of the
reforms that the international community
expects. I consider it fair to grant two
permanent seats to the African continent
with population of more than 1 billion
people and one permanent seat to Latin
Latin America.
Today the world has changed. At the same
time a number of developed countries
have also expressed their aspiration to
become members of the security council.
I believe that the request of these
countries should be also considered.
Another issue in my view the weakness of
effective mechanisms for ensuring the
implementation of the decisions of the
organization.
The systematic failure to implement the
organization's decisions undermines the
legitimacy of multilateralism concept
creates the impression that
international law is not binding and
encourages disregard for international
obligations.
Therefore, we must expand and strengthen
the authority of the United Nations. In
this regard, we propose to develop the
United Nations mechanism for the
implementation of decisions and
accountability.
First, it is necessary to establish
within the framework of the general
assembly the permanent public registry
of the implementation of resolutions and
obligations by member states. This
registry could include the following
information and ensure the
implementation of such mechanisms as
first systematically record and verify
the level of implementation of adopted
decisions.
Second, establish the obligation for
member states to regularly submit report
in accordance with the agreed standards.
Third, provide analytical
uh reviews on sectors and regions.
Fourth, ensure transparency and equal
access to information for all states.
The registry could be administered by
the United Nations Secretariat with the
support of independent experts.
If decisions of the organization are
systematically not implemented, I
propose the gradual response mechanisms.
The first stage, an official
notification to the concerned state
followed by consultations with the
relevant bodies of the organization. The
second stage development of a monitoring
mission to the country concerned to
assess the objective obstacles
preventing the implementation of the
decision and to prepare recommendations.
The third stage consideration of the
case right here at a plenary meeting of
the general assembly to determine the
status of the concerned state in terms
of its systematic implementation or
non-implementation of United Nations
decisions. The fourth stage, the
initiation of appropriate procedures
under the charter of the United Nations
with regard to states that fail to
comply with the requirements. In
particular, the merit could be referred
to the international to the United
Nations Security Council for
consideration of restrictive measures
provide for the international law,
including the first temporary
restriction on participation in United
Nations programs. The second
recommendations to review existing
formats of cooperation and other
diplomatic measures where appropriate.
Distinguished colleagues,
I believe that when cases of systematic
non-implementation of United Nations
decisions are considered, the permanent
members of the security council should
voluntarily refrain from using the veto.
If a mechanism designed to ensure the
implementation of the organization's
decisions is systematically blocked by
permanent members through the use of the
veto, such practice would no longer be
consistent with the spirit of the UN
charter and the principle of equal
responsibility of member states.
Therefore, we should once again consider
the possibility of voluntarily
restraining to use the veto in matters
related to the implementation of the
organization's decisions.
This approach could promote
universality, the um equality of all
states regardless of their size, the
primacy of diplomacy and avoid the
double standards. In order to implement
this initiative, I propose establishing
to open a working group with the general
assembly with the participation of the
interested member states. The working
group could conduct intergovernmental
consultations and prepare a report on
possible models for the proposed
mechanism. Following these
consultations, the general assembly and
the security council should consider
adopting the relevant resolutions and
decisions. The strategic objective of
this initiative is to ensure that the
decisions of the organization are
treated not merely as political
recommendations but as genuine
international obligations. Improvement
of their implementation would strengthen
the rule of international law and
reinforce confidence in the United
Nations. Kyrgyzstan is ready to initiate
interstate discussions on the
development of such a mechanism.
Starting from the 1st January 2027, as a
member of the United Nations Security
Council, we intend to formally submit
all these proposals to the relevant
committee.
Distinguished colleagues, I would like
to address separately uh the issues of
sanctions. As we have all observed
today's sanctions are in some cases used
by individual countries as an instrument
to interference to the international
affairs of sovereign states. The
negative consequences of unjustified
unilateral sanctions also affect small
countries such as ours which are at the
stage of formation and development. In
some cases, such practices led to
interference into the internal affairs
of independent states and contradict to
the fundamental principles of
international law. Some major states in
pursuit of their own interest put
pressure on smaller countries such as
Kyrgyzstan attempting to force them to
bargain over certain matters and issuing
ultimatums.
In these contexts, I would like to take
this opportunity tonight to note that
the decision made by the president of
the United States, his excellency Mr.
Donald Trump, after taking office to
hold funding of non-governmental
organizations around the world. As a
result, interference by NOS's in the
internal affairs and policies of the
developing countries has practically
seized. President Trump's decisions have
created conditions for strengthening the
sovereignty of states and enabling them
to independently choose their own path
of development. Therefore, taking this
opportunity, I would like to express my
appreciation to Mr. Trump for ending the
founding of the NOS's.
Distinguished colleagues,
decisions to impose sanctions should be
taken in accordance with the UN charter
and the exclusively within the mandate
of the security council. We believe that
the mandate to impose sanctions against
the state should belong exclusively to
the United Nations. In my view, this is
the only possible way to improve the
international sanctions system. First
and foremost, we should introduce a
mandatory mechanisms under which all
sanction and measures are reviewed in
advance by organization. The prior
review of sanction would help ensure
that their potential humanitarian,
economic and social consequences are
taken into account. An important element
of the proposed mechanism should be the
enhanced transparency and
accountability.
States initiating sanctions should
clearly indicate the legal basis for
such measures, explain their necessity
and objectives and define clear criteria
and conditions for their eventual
removal. I believe it would be
appropriate to establish under the opice
of the United Nations the unified
international mechanism for monitoring
sanctions and reviewing them on a
regular basis. Only then can the central
role of the United Nations in
maintaining international peace and
security be strengthened and its mandate
enhanced.
This would also help eliminate the risk
the sanctions being used arbitrarily by
one country against another for
political or economic gain. No state
should act arbitrarily.
The United Nations must be strong. Every
country should tremble than the United
Nations intends to impose sanctions.
Only then the strict international order
can be established in the world.
Otherwise, some decisions of the United
Nations may no longer be taken seriously
while states simply act according to
their own discretion. Every decision of
the United Nations should be implemented
without delay. If a state fails to
implement such decisions and other
countries seize cooperation with it, the
effectiveness of sanctions will increase
only then where decision will be
implemented promptly and the United
Nations will become a strong and
respected organization. Otherwise,
existing sanction will become sort of
children's toy. Dear friends, as you
know, climate change has become a global
challenge. The average temperature of
our planet and the number of climate
related emergencies are rising rapidly.
where then a negative impact on energy,
agriculture, food security and the
economy as a whole has reached a
significant scale.
Kyrgyzstan is a mountainous country. We
are particularly vulnerable to effect of
melting glaciers and this is not an
abstract threat. It is an environmental
challenge of the regional significance.
I believe it is extremely important and
necessary to unite international efforts
in addressing climate challenges and the
problems facing mountainous regions. In
this regard, in 21st 23rd October 2027,
Bishkak will host the second global
mountain summit Bishkek plus 25. Taking
this opportunity, I invite all of you to
participate in the summit. The summit
will serve as the concluding event for
the five years of action for the
development of mountain regions for 2023
2027 term.
During my meeting with United Nations
Secretary General Mr. Antonio Bishke on
31st August 2026, I proposed organizing
this summit jointly with the
organization.
These efforts demonstrate our country's
leading role among mountain states and
its commitment to unite international
efforts to address their challenges.
Therefore, Kyrgyzstan stands fully ready
to serve with the United Nations as the
voice of small and developing countries
in addressing the climate related
challenges affecting mountainous
regions. Distinguished heads of
delegations, continuing the topic of
climate change, I would like to draw
your attention to another environmental
challenge. As we all know, global
problems and disasters often have their
origins at the local level.
The issue concerns the unique high
altitude lake is which is the part of
the UNESCO biosphere reserve and is
included among wetlands of international
importance under the Ramsar framework.
Today this invaluable natural water
reservoir is under severe climatic
stress. Over the past 170 years, the
water level has fallen by almost 14
meters, while over the past five years,
the rate of decline has reached
approximately 7 cm per year.
101 rivers historically flowed into the
lake, but today only 30 flow throughout
the entire year. The main source of
water for Lake Isul is the glacier of
the Tianan mountains. Over the past 70
years, more than 30% of the region mount
mountain glaciers have melted. Nearly
20% of this reduction has occurred
within the just past 7 to 10 years. This
process poses a direct threat to the
biodiversity of the region and economic
stability of hundreds of thousands of
people. As part of our efforts to
preserve Lake Isul, Kyrgystan is
mobilizing all available domestic
resources. In particular, the state
concept for the sustainable development
of the SQL ecological and economic
system until 2030 is being implemented.
Strict environmental restrictions have
been introduced and pilot projects have
been launched to monitor the depths of
the lake using the underwater robotic
technologies. Large-scale efforts to
clean the lake bed and its waters are
continuing on a regular b basis. The
scale and speed of climate change exceed
the capacity of any individual mountain
country and require consolidated
international action. The loss of Lake
Isle would not be merely a local
tragedy. It would become an irreversible
environmental loss for the entire
region. In order to understand the
potential scale of this environmental
challenge and the cost association with
preventing, it is important to look at
the fate of the RLC and lake chart, both
of which have suffered severely over
recent decades.
Please take a look at
not so long ago, the RLC and Lake Chart
just like today were full and reservoir
was full of water. Today they have
largely dried up.
For us, this example must serve as a
clear warning. Taking this opportunity,
I officially call upon the United
Nations International Financial
Institutions and donor countries to
support our initiative to establish
under the opice of the organization the
special joint trust fund for the
preservation of Lake Isle. In order to
demonstrate our commitments through
concrete actions, we are prepared to
contribute 10 million US dollars from
the state budget to this fund. In our
culture, there is a concept known as
ammanat. It means the duty to carefully
preserve what our ancestors have
entrusted to us and to pass it on to
future generations. In this sense, it
would be fair to state that legacy is
our shared climate ammon. We are not
asking for help. We are proposing a
joint global partnership to preserve
this unique natural resource for the
earth. Before it is too late, let us
unite our efforts and resources within
the framework of this trust fund.
Distinguished participants, ladies and
gentlemen, the challenges before us are
shared. Therefore, our response to them
must be also collective. We stand at the
threshold of a new era of change.
safe, just and sustainable future can be
built only through collective action.
The destiny of our planet and future
generations is the responsibility of
each and every one of us. This year,
Kyrgystan celebrates the 31st
anniversary of its independence.
Throughout this period, our country has
faced many different challenges. Since
then, we chose cooperation over
confrontation, creation over
destruction, and embark upon the path of
sustainable development. There is one
thing we must all remember. Peace does
not come about by itself. Therefore, let
us turn our words into action, concrete
steps that improve people's lives and
protect nature. Let us build together a
world which dialect is stronger than
weapons. Mutual respect is stronger than
fear and cooperation among nations
delivers tangible results for all
humanity.
Thank you very much for your attention.
On behalf of the assembly, I wish to
thank the president of the Kirgis
Republic.
